verdict.rationale:
Buzz issues each agent its own Nostr keypair as a distinct credential/identity (buzz-supp-acp-harness, buzz-gh-4), with a dedicated agent-authentication spec (NIP-AA) that scopes agent access to owner enrollment and auto-revokes when the owner's membership is revoked (buzz-supp-nip-aa-agent-auth), a fail-closed owned-agent discovery model where discovery alone does not confer authorization (buzz-supp-owned-agent-guardrails), and an admin API that requires signed per-request events rather than static tokens with a two-tier principal model (buzz-supp-admin-api). Git access is similarly scoped to the agent's own keypair rather than a shared PAT (buzz-supp-git-nostr-credentials).

missing for 10: independent/hands-on validation of real-world least-privilege enforcement (community members flag that the group/permission rules may not survive real-world edge cases, e.g. buzz-comm-6), and no documented fine-grained per-API-scope (read/write/admin) system beyond channel membership + admin tiers.
